name: Silver Ticket - Forge Service Ticket (mimikatz)
description: Forge a Kerberos service ticket (TGS) for any service using the service account's NT hash — without ever contacting the KDC. Unlike a golden ticket (forged TGT), a silver ticket is a forged TGS for a specific service on a specific host. It is signed with the service account's NT hash, so the DC is never involved after the initial domain info is gathered. Grants access to the target service as any user, including Domain Admin, with no network traffic to the DC.
source: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 22: Attacking Active Directory Authentication (22.2.4)

# mssql      -> SQL Server
# wsman      -> WinRM / PowerShell remoting

notes: Silver tickets are stealthier than golden tickets because they never touch the DC — no 4768/4769 Kerberos events are generated at the DC level. The ticket is encrypted with the service account's NT hash (RC4 by default; /aes256 if you have the AES key). The /user field can be any string (even non-existent users); the service trusts the ticket because it's validly signed. To target CIFS: /service:cifs allows access to file shares. Silver tickets expire after 10 years by default (mimikatz default) so they persist across reboots. Requires: (1) domain SID — get from whoami /user or Get-DomainSID; (2) service account NT hash — dump via sekurlsa::logonpasswords on a host where the service account has a session.

recommended.note: Need the service account NT hash from sekurlsa::logonpasswords before forging.
kerberos::ptt imports an existing .kirbi ticket; silver ticket forges one in memory directly.
Silver ticket for LDAP service grants DCSync rights — forge /service:ldap then run dcsync.

defense.why_it_works: Silver tickets are forged Kerberos service tickets (TGS) created with the target service account's NTLM hash. Mimikatz kerberos::golden /service:cifs creates a forged TGS for the specified service — no KDC interaction needed. The service validates the ticket with its own key, accepting it as legitimate. Useful for persistent, stealthy access to a specific service.
defense.prerequisites: NTLM hash of the target service account (from Kerberoasting or Mimikatz). Domain SID. Service SPN. Target FQDN. Mimikatz for ticket creation and injection.
defense.impact: T1558.002 Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Silver Ticket. Persistent authenticated access to a specific service without KDC interaction. DA-equivalent access to the targeted service. No 4768/4769 events on DC — stealthier than Golden Tickets.
defense.detection:
Event 4624 on target host with Kerberos auth but no prior 4769 on DC. MDI: 'Suspected Kerberos forged ticket (silver ticket)'. PAC validation (if enabled) contacts DC and detects forged PAC. Anomalous service access from unexpected source IPs.
Anomalous Kerberos activity: forged or stolen tickets by correlating malformed fields in logon events, RC4-encrypted TGTs, or TGS requests without corresponding TGT requests; suspicious processes accessing LSASS memory for ticket extraction (DET0522/AN1443).
Suspicious access to SSSD secrets database and Kerberos key material indicating ticket theft or replay; correlate anomalous file access with unusual Kerberos service ticket requests (AN1444).
Forging or replaying Kerberos tickets: monitor Unified Logs for anomalous kinit/klist activity and unusual authentication sequences (AN1445).
defense.artifacts: Event 4624 type 3 on target with no prior DC 4769 | MDI: silver ticket alert | Missing 4769 on DC for the session | PAC validation failure log (if enabled)
defense.prevention:
gMSA for service accounts (auto-rotating passwords — forged silver tickets expire with rotation). PAC validation on services. MDI deployment. Rotate service account passwords immediately when Kerberoasted.
Active Directory Configuration: Reset KRBTGT account password twice (invalidates all golden tickets); rotate every 180 days.
Audit: Scan for insecure Kerberos configurations.
Credential Access Protection: On Linux, use SELinux to protect Kerberos key material.
Encrypt Sensitive Information: Enable AES Kerberos encryption instead of RC4.
Password Policies: Service accounts should have 25+ character passwords; use Group Managed Service Accounts (gMSA).
Privileged Account Management: Limit domain admin to DCs only; restrict service account privileges.
defense.evasion: Only works for the specific service/host — targeted, stealthy. No DC logs. Use for persistent access to specific servers rather than broad domain movement.
defense.misconfiguration: Service accounts with stale NTLM hashes (Kerberoastable). PAC validation disabled. gMSA not used. No monitoring for Kerberos auth without prior DC exchange.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Stale service account hash (Kerberoasted and cracked):
# svc_mssql password 'Sql@2019' — unchanged since 2019
# Silver ticket forged for MSSQLSvc/sql01.corp.local
# → Full DB access as 'Administrator' with no DC events

# PAC validation off (default):
(Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa').ValidateKdcPacSignature  # null = off
defense.secure_config:
# gMSA for all service accounts:
New-ADServiceAccount -Name svc_mssql -DNSHostName sql.corp.local -ManagedPasswordIntervalInDays 30

# Enable PAC validation:
Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa' -Name ValidateKdcPacSignature -Value 1

# MDI: silver ticket detection enabled by default
